title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, workplaces and studies, and say what you can, can't, have to and must do.
intro:
आप क्या करते हैं? 'What do you do?' is one of the first questions Indians ask. In this unit you'll learn jobs, the office and school vocabulary, and how to talk about them.

The grammar is all about **modality**: 'I **can** speak Hindi' (**बोल सकता हूँ**), 'I **know how** to drive' (**मुझे गाड़ी चलाना आता है**), 'I **have to** go' (**मुझे जाना है**), and 'I'm **forced** to work late' (**मुझे देर तक काम करना पड़ता है**).

vocab.note: f · नौकरी करना 'to have a job'
m/f · formal: अध्यापक (m), अध्यापिका (f); respectful: गुरु जी, सर, मैडम
m · f: छात्रा · also विद्यार्थी vidyārthī, 'स्टूडेंट'
Always after a verb stem: कर सकना

vocab.en: to manage to; to get, find
vocab.note: Usually in the negative: नहीं आ पाया 'couldn't make it'

grammar.title: Can: सकना, आना and पाना
grammar.body:
**सकना** = 'can, be able'. It never stands alone: put it after the **stem** of the main verb and conjugate सकना like any verb:

मैं हिंदी **बोल सकता हूँ** 'I can speak Hindi' · वह नहीं **आ सकती** 'she can't come' · क्या मैं बैठ सकता हूँ? 'may I sit?'

**आना** for **learned skills** ('know how to'): dative + infinitive + आना. The verb agrees with the skill (usually masculine आता): **मुझे तैरना आता है** 'I can swim', **उसे हिंदी आती है** 'he/she knows Hindi' (हिंदी f).

**पाना** = 'manage to', mostly negative, for circumstances getting in the way: **मैं सो नहीं पाया** 'I couldn't (manage to) sleep'.

examples.roman: maiṃ thoṛī hindī paṛh saktī hūṃ.
examples.en: I can read a little Hindi. (woman)

examples.en: I couldn't study because of the noise. (woman)

grammar.title: Have to / must: है, पड़ना, चाहिए
grammar.body:
All three use the **dative** (मुझे, आपको…) + **infinitive**:

**infinitive + है** — a plan or personal need, 'I have to / I need to / I'm supposed to': **मुझे जाना है** 'I have to go'. This is the everyday one.

**infinitive + पड़ना** — compulsion from outside, 'I'm forced to / I end up having to': **मुझे जाना पड़ेगा** 'I'll have to go', **मुझे जाना पड़ता है** 'I (always) have to go', **मुझे जाना पड़ा** 'I had to go'.

**infinitive + चाहिए** — advice, 'should' (Unit 9): **मुझे जाना चाहिए** 'I should go'.

Negatives: **मुझे नहीं जाना है** 'I don't want to/have to go'; **जाने की ज़रूरत नहीं है** 'there's no need to go'.

dialogue.title: A job interview
dialogue.setting: Rahul is interviewing for a job at a travel company in Mumbai. The manager, Mrs Iyer, asks the questions.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: नमस्ते मैडम। क्या मैं अंदर आ सकता हूँ?
lines.roman: namaste maiḍam. kyā maiṃ andar ā saktā hūṃ?
lines.en: Hello madam. May I come in?

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: हाँ, आइए, बैठिए। तो, आप अभी क्या करते हैं?
lines.roman: hāṃ, āiye, baiṭhiye. to, āp abhī kyā karte haiṃ?
lines.en: Yes, come in, sit down. So, what do you do at the moment?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: मैं एक होटल में काम करता हूँ। पर मुझे रात को काम करना पड़ता है।
lines.roman: maiṃ ek hoṭal meṃ kām kartā hūṃ. par mujhe rāt ko kām karnā paṛtā hai.
lines.en: I work in a hotel. But I have to work nights.

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: आप कौन-कौन सी भाषाएँ बोल सकते हैं?
lines.roman: āp kaun-kaun sī bhāṣāyeṃ bol sakte haiṃ?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: हिंदी, मराठी और अंग्रेज़ी। और मैं थोड़ी फ़्रेंच भी सीख रहा हूँ।
lines.roman: hindī, marāṭhī aur aṅgrezī. aur maiṃ thoṛī french bhī sīkh rahā hūṃ.
lines.en: Hindi, Marathi and English. And I'm learning a bit of French too.

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: बहुत अच्छा। इस नौकरी में आपको बहुत यात्रा करनी पड़ेगी।
lines.roman: bahut achchhā. is naukrī meṃ āpko bahut yātrā karnī paṛegī.
lines.en: Very good. In this job you'll have to travel a lot.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: कोई बात नहीं, मुझे घूमना बहुत पसंद है।
lines.roman: koī bāt nahīṃ, mujhe ghūmnā bahut pasand hai.

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: क्या आपको गाड़ी चलाना आता है?
lines.roman: kyā āpko gāṛī chalānā ātā hai?
lines.en: Do you know how to drive?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: जी हाँ, मेरे पास लाइसेंस भी है।
lines.roman: jī hāṃ, mere pās lāisens bhī hai.
lines.en: Yes, and I have a licence too.

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: ठीक है। आपका कोई सवाल है?
lines.roman: ṭhīk hai. āpkā koī savāl hai?
lines.en: Alright. Do you have any questions?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: जी, मुझे कब तक जवाब मिल सकता है?
lines.roman: jī, mujhe kab tak javāb mil saktā hai?
lines.en: Yes — by when could I hear back?

lines.speaker: Mrs Iyer
lines.native: अगले हफ़्ते तक। हम आपको फ़ोन करेंगे।
lines.roman: agle hafte tak. ham āpko fon kareṃge.
lines.en: By next week. We'll call you.

culture: Education is taken very seriously in India; board exams in 10th and 12th grade (दसवीं, बारहवीं) are major family events, and coaching classes are a huge industry. Teachers are highly respected — students address them as **सर** and **मैडम** (or गुरु जी), and stand when they enter. In offices, people commonly use **जी** after names or 'सर/मैडम' for seniors; first names alone are used among peers. Office Hindi is heavily mixed with English: मीटिंग, डेडलाइन, प्रोजेक्ट, बॉस are all normal Hindi words now.

lessons.title: What can you do?

tip.title: सकना — can
tip.body:
- Put **सकना** after the verb **stem**: मैं बोल **सकता** हूँ 'I can speak', वह नहीं आ **सकती** 'she can't come'.
- It changes like any verb: **सकता** (m), **सकती** (f), **सकते** (pl / आप).
- A skill you know how to do: **मुझे** खाना बनाना **आता है**.
- **पाना** 'manage to', mostly negative: मैं नहीं आ **पाया** 'I couldn't make it'.

lessons.title: Things I have to do

tip.title: मुझे जाना है — I have to go
tip.body:
- **मुझे + verb-ना + है**: a plan or need — मुझे जाना **है** 'I have to go'.
- **+ पड़ना**: forced by circumstances — मुझे जाना **पड़ता है** 'I (always) have to go', **पड़ा** 'I had to'.
- **+ चाहिए**: advice — मुझे जाना **चाहिए** 'I should go'.
- The person always takes **मुझे / आपको / उसे**.
tip.pattern: मुझे + verb-ना + है / पड़ता है / चाहिए
